author: John Baker
title: Harvard Suffers Blow Over Visa Misuse Allegations - NewsBreak
text: Harvard University has submitted I-9 Employment Eligibility Verification forms for staff in response to demands from the Trump administration. The action follows allegations regarding foreign students misusing their visas and inciting violence, which have resulted in funding cuts and legal challenges. Reports have indicated that Harvard may allocate up to $500 million to settle disputes with the Trump administration. Harvard University stated, “We are evaluating the government’s position on whether the Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act (FERPA) permits disclosure of those records.” Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem said, “If Harvard won’t defend the interests of its students, then we will. We tried to do things the easy way with Harvard.” Noem added, “Now, through their refusal to cooperate, we have to do things the hard way. Harvard, like other universities, has allowed foreign students to abuse their visa privileges and advocate for violence and terrorism on campus.” Harvard refused administrative demands to curb activism and dismantle DEI programs. In response to pro-Palestinian protests, the administration accused universities of enabling antisemitism and retaliated by cutting $2.6 billion in research grants and canceling federal contracts. Justice Department lawyer Michael Velchik said, “Harvard prioritized campus protestors over cancer research.” District Judge Allison Burroughs (D-OK), overseeing the case, has questioned the justification for cutting funding and raised concerns about free speech violations. A ruling is expected soon. Burroughs said, “That’s a major stumbling block for me.” She added, “If you can make this decision, that we’re going to withdraw all this funding for reasons oriented around speech, the consequences to that, in terms of constitutional law, are staggering to me.” John Baker covers U.S. politics & news for content partner Modern Newsstand LLC.
